_comment_id: REPLACE-ME. A short name for this endpoint. It appears in the daemon's configuration and in the source string of each registered entry. It is printed, so keep it boring — 'provider', not the company name and not an account identifier.
_comment_shape: EXACTLY ONE OF resolverUrl OR directBaseUrl. The product uses the resolver whenever one is present, so setting both would leave the other as silently dead configuration — preflight refuses that rather than picking for you.
_comment_resolver: OPTIONAL. An https endpoint that exchanges a stable objectRef for short-lived access material. Use this when your provider issues expiring signed URLs. The gate POSTs {"objectRef": "..."} with the credential sent in the bearer-scheme Authorization header, and expects {"url": "...", "headers": {...}} back. Leave as null if your provider serves references directly.
_comment_direct: OPTIONAL. An https base URL the stable reference is appended to as ONE path segment. Use this when your provider serves a durable URL per object. Leave as null if you set resolverUrl.
_comment_origins: REQUIRED, AND NEVER EMPTY. The egress allowlist, as scheme+host+port. A resolved URL whose origin is not on this list is never contacted — which is what stops a signed URL, or a redirect, steering the daemon somewhere you never authorised. Empty is not permissive here; it is refused. List every origin your provider may legitimately hand back, and nothing else.
_comment_switches: BOTH OF THESE MUST STAY FALSE FOR A REAL RUN, and preflight refuses either one set. They are fixture switches. allowInsecureHttp would send a real credential, in the clear, over plaintext HTTP. allowPrivateAddresses would authorise the daemon to dial loopback and link-local addresses — which against a real provider means a redirect could steer it at the host's own metadata service. They are two separate permissions in the product precisely because deriving one from the other was a bug.
